annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Chaos Mesh experiment ~133 min ago knocked all 3 Kafka brokers offline simultaneously; all pods are back Running/Ready, but broker-0's metrics exporter is wedged (not scrapeable), keeping the KafkaBrokerDown alert firing. The cluster is functionally healthy (0 offline partitions, 0 under-min-ISR) but has 60 under-replicated partitions still catching up and no visible active-controller metric (because broker-0, likely the KRaft controller, is not being scraped).
diagnosis.root_cause: A Chaos Mesh deployment (revision 9187ff9e9e6f, ~133 minutes ago) triggered a chaos experiment that simultaneously terminated all three Kafka broker pods with exit code 255 (Unknown). All three restarted and are Kubernetes-Ready, but broker lakehouse-dual-role-0's JMX/Prometheus metrics endpoint has been unreachable since it came back up (~129 minutes ago). Prometheus therefore counts only 2 reachable brokers, sustaining the KafkaBrokerDown alert. The 0 active_controllers metric is a secondary symptom: broker-0 is likely the active KRaft controller, so its controller count metric is also missing from scrapes.
diagnosis.impact: Data pipeline is currently safe: 0 offline partitions, 0 partitions below min.insync.replicas=2, Flink job is RUNNING/STABLE. However, 60 partitions remain under-replicated (replication catchup in progress), the cluster has no failure margin (one more broker loss would halt writes), and the missing active-controller metric means controller health is unobservable. Flink consumer lag is 200 messages — minor, consistent with the brief outage.

evidence.finding: All 3 broker pods Running 1/1; lakehouse-dual-role-0 brokers_scraped_up=false, brokers 1 and 2 scraped_up=true. under_replicated_partitions=60, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=0.0. All 3 brokers last_termination ~129 minutes ago with reason=Unknown exit_code=255.
All 4 nodes Ready, no pressure conditions, no unschedulable taints. Workers spread across zone-a, zone-b, zone-c — no zone failure.
chaos-mesh-local deployed revision 9187ff9e9e6f 133.1 minutes ago — directly preceding the broker crash times (~129 min ago). This is the most likely trigger of the multi-broker outage.
Flink job events-to-iceberg is RUNNING/STABLE, started 127.9 minutes ago (auto-recovered after broker outage). Checkpoints succeeding (28.23/5m), no failed checkpoints, consumer_lag=200.
KafkaBrokerDown is still actively firing (0.9 min). No other Kafka or Flink alerts firing.
Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: Strimzi restarts crashed brokers automatically; if pod is Running but unhealthy, check logs and metrics port. Do not delete PVC.
Zero warning events in kafka namespace in the last 180 minutes — no PVC, volume, or scheduling issues logged.

proposed_action.rationale: Broker-0 has been Running/Ready for ~129 minutes but its metrics endpoint has been unresponsive the entire time — a classic wedged JMX exporter state. The alert will not clear until broker-0 is scrapeable. Restarting the pod via Strimzi (delete → automatic recreation) will reinitialise the JMX exporter. It is safe now: under_min_isr_partitions=0 and offline_partitions=0 mean the cluster can tolerate one broker going briefly offline. The PVC is not touched, so broker-0 will rejoin with its existing log data and minimise re-replication. Recommend waiting for the 60 under-replicated partitions to drop to 0 first if possible, to avoid any added replication pressure.

follow_ups: Wait for under_replicated_partitions to reach 0 before restarting broker-0, to minimize replication overhead during the restart.
Investigate the Chaos Mesh experiment (revision 9187ff9e9e6f deployed ~133 min ago) — confirm it was intentional and scheduled. If unintended, the chaos schedule should be reviewed or suspended.
After broker-0 restarts, verify active_controllers returns to 1 to confirm KRaft controller election is healthy.
Review why all 3 brokers were terminated simultaneously — a properly scoped chaos experiment should target at most 1 broker at a time given RF=3 / min-ISR=2.
Monitor Flink consumer lag (currently 200) to confirm it drains after broker-0 recovers.
The OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing alert (firing 42.7 min) indicates the ops agent has had recent investigation failures — review its logs separately.
